CHIEF COMPLAINT
Patient presents requesting assistance with smoking cessation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old male with nicotine dependence presenting with strong motivation to quit smoking. He has been smoking since high school, beginning with experimentation at social events. Over time, smoking became a daily habit and he now smokes 1.5 packs per day, with first cigarette within one hour of waking. He previously attempted to quit using cold turkey method and was successful for approximately one year, but relapsed due to work-related stress (workplace layoffs with resultant increased responsibilities). Currently motivated by impending fatherhood—daughter expected to be born imminently. He is interested in using nicotine patch based on friends' reported success. Patient recently joined gym and started meditation practice as stress management strategies. Planned quit date is next Monday, coinciding with patient's birthday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes
History of gout
Cardiac murmur (2/6 systolic murmur, previously noted, stable)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
44-year-old married male, expecting daughter. Tobacco use: 1.5 packs cigarettes daily x many years, no other tobacco products. Recent lifestyle changes include gym membership and meditation practice. Employed, recently experienced workplace stress related to staff reductions.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 128/88, heart rate 68, respirations 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated (known, unchanged)
Pulmonary: Lungs clear and equal bilaterally, no expiratory wheezes, no rales or rhonchi
Neck: No lymphadenopathy; no carotid bruits appreciated

RESULTS
Vitals as documented above. Hemoglobin A1c ordered for follow-up laboratory work.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine Dependence: Start 21 mg nicotine patch on quit date (next Monday). Change patch location daily to minimize skin irritation. Taper dose over time with close follow-up; no fixed tapering schedule. Continue gym routine and stress management including meditation and yoga. Monitor stress triggers related to work and upcoming birth of child. Provided smoking cessation handouts. Return visit in 2 weeks to reassess and adjust dosage as needed.

2. Type 2 Diabetes: Continue management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c to be drawn at next visit in 2 weeks; results to be discussed at follow-up.

3. History of Gout: Continue allopurinol. Continue monitoring dietary triggers that elevate uric acid levels.

4. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks.
